# Building the Future: Inside Astec’s Inaugural Young Executive Seminar


The future of the manufacturing industry won’t be shaped by equipment alone. It…


November 25, 2026


Share:


The future of the manufacturing industry won’t be shaped by equipment alone. It will be shaped by the people making decisions, solving challenges, and leading organizations through a rapidly evolving business landscape. That’s why Astec created the Young Executive Seminar (YES).


Emerging leaders from across our industry gathered for the inaugural Young Executive Seminar, an event designed to invest in the next generation of leadership. Over several days, attendees engaged in meaningful discussions around leadership, business strategy, workforce development, innovation, and the future of the industries that build and connect our communities.


> *“I look forward to putting what I learned into play and appreciate the opportunity to be part of such a powerful event.”*
>
>
> **— Stephen Luccarelli, RCA Asphalt**


**More Than a Seminar**


The Young Executive Seminar is intentionally designed to be more than a series of presentations. It’s an opportunity for attendees to step away from the day-to-day demands of business and focus on bigger questions:


- Where is the industry headed?
- What challenges will define the next decade?
- How can organizations attract and retain the workforce needed for future growth?
- What role will technology, automation, and data play in driving productivity?
- What does effective leadership look like in a changing business environment?


Throughout the event, participants engaged directly with industry experts and peers who brought diverse experiences and perspectives to the conversation. The result was an environment where ideas could be challenged, lessons could be shared, and meaningful dialogue could take place.


> *“I left feeling energized, inspired, and even more excited about the future of our industry.”*
> **— Katie Peabody, Lakeside Industries, Inc.**


**Learning from Industry Leaders**


A key component of the inaugural Young Executive Seminar was direct access to accomplished leaders from both within and beyond our industry. Through candid discussions and real-world examples, attendees gained practical insights they can apply throughout their careers.


Participants explored the power of culture with Mark Gliebe, Chairman of Astec’s Board of Directors and former CEO of Regal Beloit Corporation, and Jeff Jackson, Astec Board Member and CEO of Cabinetworks Group, while Aletheia Silcott, CHRO at Astec, challenged attendees to define their personal leadership philosophy.


Emerging leaders also gained valuable perspectives on business growth and market dynamics from Kathryn Thompson, Founder and CEO of Thompson Research Group, and Christina Bresani, Head of Mid-Cap Mergers & Acquisitions at Wells Fargo. Practical financial and business insights were shared by Michael Bell, CFO of C.W. Matthews, and Brian Harris, CFO of Astec.


As attendees explored the broader forces shaping the future of the asphalt, aggregates, concrete, and road building sectors, Michele Stanley, President and CEO of the National Stone, Sand & Gravel Association (NSSGA), and Nile Elam, Vice President of Government Affairs at the National Asphalt Pavement Association (NAPA), provided valuable perspective on the policies, trends, and challenges impacting construction materials businesses today.


Additionally, the seminar included a customer-focused perspective from Jimmy Patton, President and CEO of Rogers Group, offering attendees firsthand insight into the priorities, opportunities, and challenges facing producers.


The learning extended beyond the meeting room with an exclusive tour of Astec’s Jerome Avenue facility. There, those in attendance experienced a behind-the-scenes look at manufacturing in action, seeing firsthand the craftsmanship, expertise, and dedication that goes into every piece of Astec equipment. The group also explored Astec Digital solutions and how connected technologies are helping customers solve unique challenges and optimize their operations. This combination of hands-on manufacturing insight and technology innovation provided young leaders with a deeper understanding of the solutions driving the industry forward.


From leadership and culture to business strategy, industry advocacy, manufacturing excellence, and digital innovation, these conversations challenged attendees to think beyond their day-to-day responsibilities while equipping them with new ideas, fresh perspectives, and practical strategies for the future.


**Investing in What’s Next**


For more than 50 years, Astec has supported the people who build, power, and connect communities around the world. The Young Executive Seminar reflects that same commitment, providing a space where emerging leaders can learn, collaborate, and prepare for the future.


As our industry continues to evolve, strong leadership will remain one of its most important assets. By bringing together ambitious professionals, experienced experts, and diverse perspectives, YES helps ensure the next generation is prepared to meet tomorrow’s challenges and seize tomorrow’s opportunities.


The future of our industry isn’t something we are waiting for. It’s something we are building together.


> *“The experience was both informative and motivating, providing valuable perspectives that I can apply throughout my career. I would highly recommend this program to other professionals across the industry.”*
> **— Emerging industry leader**

## About Astec


Since 1972, Astec Industries, Inc. has been connecting communities by providing innovative rock to road solutions for our customers. United by our purpose – Built to Connect – Astec is a leading global manufacturer of specialized equipment for asphalt road building, aggregate processing and concrete production. Operations are divided into two primary business segments. Infrastructure Solutions includes road building, asphalt and concrete plants, thermal and storage solutions. Materials Solutions includes aggregate and other material processing solutions. For more information, follow us on social media.
